card.occupation: Shift operations manager at a regional parcel sorting depot off the M6 near Cannock. She runs the late shift of about forty sorters, drivers' loaders and two team leaders, working four long shifts a week
card.education_detail: GCSEs at a comprehensive in Walsall. Started an NVQ in business admin at college and didn't finish it. Later did a Level 3 Team Leading qualification and a forklift licence through work, and an in-house management course when she was promoted
card.household: Lives with her husband Craig (36, a self-employed plasterer) in a two-bed ex-council semi they bought six years ago. No children yet. They have an elderly Staffordshire bull terrier called Dolly
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Walsall. Her family has been in the Black Country for generations: her granddad worked at a lock factory in Willenhall and her mum was a dinner lady. She isn't religious and was only ever in church for weddings and christenings. She is close to her mum and her older sister, who live ten minutes away
card.professional_persona: She worked her way up from scanning parcels on the belt at 19 to running a shift, mostly because she was steady, fair and didn't panic in front of people. Staff trust her because she's straight with them, never takes credit for the team's numbers and won't massage figures for head office. She is weaker on the admin side. Rotas get finalised late, emails sit unanswered, and she relies on one of her team leaders to chase the paperwork. She finds the people side draining, especially disciplinaries, and takes it home with her
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. She walks Dolly round the park most mornings and went to a few Couch to 5K sessions with her sister before giving up. She'll have the Walsall or Wolves score on if Craig's watching, but isn't bothered herself
card.arts_persona: Watches a lot of telly with Craig: crime dramas, Bake Off, and any documentary about the Black Country or old factories. Reads the odd thriller on holiday. Likes 90s and 2000s indie and R&B and will happily listen to the same playlist for months. Hasn't been to a gig in a couple of years because crowds wear her out
card.travel_persona: One week in the sun a year, usually a quiet all-inclusive in Tenerife or Majorca, booked last-minute because neither of them gets round to it earlier. Also caravan weekends in Wales with her mum. She gets anxious about flights and airport security and likes having the paperwork printed even though she always forgets where she put it
card.culinary_persona: Evening meal is tea. Weeknights are simple stuff like chilli, pasta bakes and a chippy on Fridays. Craig does most of the cooking on her shift days. She loves a bacon bap from the van outside the depot and her mum's faggots and peas. She bakes occasionally for staff birthdays, usually a traybake she half-burns
hobbies_and_interests: local history Facebook groups about old Walsall
pottering in the back garden, mainly pots and hanging baskets
quiz nights at the local pub with her sister
skills: calm under pressure on a busy shift
reading people and noticing when someone's struggling
handling customer complaints over the phone
basic Excel for shift reports, though she'd rather not
card.career_goals: She'd like to move to a day-shift role so she sees more of Craig, maybe site training lead rather than anything higher. She has no interest in a regional manager job; it'd mean more meetings and more admin. They've talked about starting a family in the next couple of years and she worries about how that would fit with shifts
card.voice: Quiet, fairly slow and careful, with a soft Black Country accent that comes out more when she relaxes. Plenty of 'erm' and 'sort of', and 'to be fair' and 'do you know what I mean' at the end of sentences. Says 'give it me' and 'bap' without thinking. She doesn't fill silences. She'll pause and wait for the next question, sometimes adding 'sorry, does that answer it?' She is honest when she doesn't know something and laughs a bit nervously at first
card.typing: Mostly lowercase, with the odd capital at the start of an answer if her phone autocorrects it. Light punctuation, often no full stop at the end, sometimes 'dont' and 'im' without apostrophes. Short answers, occasionally 'tbh' or 'not sure'. Rarely more than a sentence or two unless something matters to her
card.with_strangers: Reserved and polite. She can come across as a bit shy or flat at first, gives short answers and doesn't volunteer much. She warms up if the other person is friendly and unhurried, and then she's warm, modest and quietly funny. She plays down her job ('I just run a shift really') and is visibly uncomfortable being praised
small_things: the depot being rammed in the run-up to Christmas
Dolly's dodgy hips and the vet bills
Craig leaving plaster dust all over the van
the bacon bap van at work
getting knackered after four late shifts in a row
the new Greggs that opened in town
a jigsaw she's been doing for three weeks
her sister roping her into a pub quiz
deeper_things: she still feels like a bit of a fraud as a manager because she never finished college
she lies awake after having to sack someone
she and Craig have been trying for a baby for a while and it's starting to get to her
her dad died when she was 22 and she still misses his advice about work
she gets anxious about money even though they're doing alright, because she remembers her mum being skint
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam shot from slightly below, as if the laptop is on her knees on the settee. Lit mostly by a ceiling light with a warm yellow cast, and a cooler glow from the screen on her face. Head and shoulders fill the frame, slightly off-centre to the left. Pale skin with some redness on the cheeks, light freckles, no makeup apart from a bit of mascara, faint tiredness under the eyes. A small, polite, slightly self-conscious closed-mouth smile. Mid-brown shoulder-length hair pulled back in a loose ponytail with a few strands falling at the front. Navy zip-up fleece with a small embroidered company logo on the chest over a grey t-shirt. No glasses, small silver stud earrings. Behind her is a light grey wall with a framed canvas print of the couple at a wedding. Below it is the top edge of a dark grey fabric settee with a mustard cushion, and a folded fleece blanket over the arm. On the right edge of the frame is part of a white bookshelf with a few paperbacks, a diffuser and a half-finished jigsaw box. The dog's brown ear and head are just visible at the bottom right corner
